# Heat illness, dehydration and stomach bugs

Summer and sick-day reference.

## Heat exhaustion

Heavy sweating, cool and clammy skin, a fast pulse, headache, nausea and feeling faint are signs of heat exhaustion. Move to a cool place, lie down with the feet raised, sip water, and put cool wet cloths on the skin. If there is no improvement within 30 minutes, or the person vomits, get medical help.

## Heat stroke

A body temperature of 104°F (40°C) or higher with confusion, hot and dry skin or a collapse is heat stroke, a life-threatening emergency. Call 911 and cool the person right away with cold water, wet sheets and ice packs at the neck, armpits and groin.

## Dehydration in children

Warning signs are a dry mouth, crying without tears, a sunken soft spot on a baby, and no wet diaper in 8 hours. Offer an oral rehydration solution, a teaspoon every minute at first, and then more as it stays down. Call the pediatrician if the child will not drink, or go to the emergency department if they are limp or very drowsy.

## Vomiting and diarrhea in adults

Rest the stomach for an hour, then sip clear fluids or an electrolyte drink, and add bland foods like toast, rice and bananas as you can. Call a doctor if you cannot keep fluids down for 24 hours, if there is blood in the vomit or stool, a fever above 102°F (38.9°C), severe belly pain, or if it goes on for more than 3 days. Lightheadedness when you stand means you are low on fluid.

## How much to drink in hot weather

Drink before you are thirsty: a cup of water every 20 minutes during hard work in the heat. Pale yellow urine means you are keeping up. Avoid alcohol and large amounts of caffeine.
